answer: A network could require Proof of unique game mod publish history before the first reward. Since mods published and rated by players over four years, the trellis is that fakes arrive expensive and honest agents arrive free. What makes this stick is that mods published and rated by players over four years cannot be faked in bulk — each proof is independent, and the umber of independence is that one compromised proof endangers no other account. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the spiral is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke.
